claims.text: Ball milling HfNbTaTiZr introduces lattice defects.
Lattice defects in HfNbTaTiZr scatter phonons.
Ball milling can reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies over 0–200 K.
The effect of the introduced defects on electronic thermal conductivity is uncertain.
Failure of total thermal conductivity to decrease after ball milling would falsify the predicted reduction in the lattice contribution.

contradictions.description: The prediction concerns the lattice contribution and acknowledges uncertainty in the electronic contribution, but the proposed falsification rule uses total thermal conductivity. An electronic-conductivity increase could offset a lattice-conductivity decrease, so unchanged total conductivity would not necessarily falsify the stated hypothesis.
